newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank association sees rates on down trend.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank association sees rates on down trend.

text.p: Italian bank interest rates are maintaining their gradual downward trend and should fall 0.45 point in the next three months, the head of the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said on Wednesday.
"Rates are falling year-on-year," Tancredi Bianci told a news conference after the group issued its monthly report.

Bianchi said the current trend confirmed his forecast of a fall of 0.15 percentage point per month. "Our rates are coming down continually and gradually. If inflation does not go up, that's the trend. In the next three months, we should see a fall of 0.45 point," he said.
The group's report said deposit rates were falling more slowly than borrowing rates because of strong competition within the system.
"In the last nine months, (deposit rates) have fallen just 0.60 point," Bianchi said.
